issues.quote: with rows equal to advertisers throughout
issues.explanation: Requiring only that rows equal distinct advertisers throughout catches fan-out joins, but passes both dropped-row steps and 1-to-1 inner joins, where rows and distinct advertisers fall together while staying equal (7,016 = 7,016 and 3,768 = 3,768). If an inner join silently deletes unmatched advertisers whose churn rate happens to be close to the dashboard rate, all four checklist items pass despite the missing customers.
issues.evidence: dirty_tables.dropna (7,016 rows, 7,016 advertisers) and dirty_tables.inner_join_drop (3,768 rows, 3,768 advertisers) both satisfy rows == advertisers; seg7 visual note states the complete rule: 'Rows should equal advertisers, and neither should change unless you asked for it.'
issues.fix: A step table: rows, distinct advertisers and churn rate after every step, with rows equal to advertisers throughout and neither count changing unless you asked to filter.

verdict: Factually accurate across all 76 numeric claims, visuals, SQL/Python examples and quiz/review items; one minor omission in the audit checklist leaves out checking that counts do not drop across steps.
